title: FIXING THE SYMPTOM, NOT THE HEART

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Esau learned that Isaac had blessed Jacob and had sent him to Paddan Aram to take a wife from there, and that when he blessed him he commanded him, 'Do not marry a Canaanite woman,' and that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and had gone to Paddan Aram. Esau then realized how displeasing the Canaanite women were to his father Isaac; so he went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth and daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham, in addition to the wives he already had." - Gen 28:6-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Esau finally notices that his Canaanite marriages had displeased his father. So he tries to make it right — he goes and marries a daughter of Ishmael, someone from within the wider family of Abraham. On the surface, it looks like an attempt to please his parents.

But look closely. Esau does not put away his existing wives or truly change his heart; he simply adds another wife "in addition to the wives he already had." He treats a deep issue as if it were a surface problem to be patched over. He adjusts his behaviour to win approval, without any real change of heart toward God.

We can do the very same thing. When we sense we have displeased God or others, our instinct is often to make a quick external fix — attend more services, adopt some religious habit, put on a better appearance — while leaving the real condition of our hearts untouched. But God is not looking mainly at our outward adjustments; He looks at the heart (1 Sam 16:7).

True change is not about patching the symptom to gain approval. It is about turning our hearts back to God in genuine repentance. Do not settle for looking better on the outside. Ask God to change you from the inside out.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I patching a symptom instead of dealing with my heart?
2. Am I seeking to please God genuinely, or just to look approved?
3. What in me needs real change, not just an outward fix?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see past my outward fixes to my heart. Do not let me settle for looking better on the surface. Change me from the inside out, in true repentance. Amen.
